title: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

sense.text: “A deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him.” That great horror is what Abraham was shown: he saw us, his seed, in ancient Egypt as slaves, being oppressed. He saw it before it ever happened.

“Thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years.” Abraham saw the children of Israel afflicted in Egypt for four hundred years.

Back in the days this scripture was used to explain America too, but this one is literally speaking of ancient Egypt: Abraham's seed afflicted in Egypt for four hundred years.

“And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge.” That nation lets you know it is speaking of back then, the nation we served. “And afterward shall they come out with great substance”, and that is what literally happened: we came out of ancient Egypt with great substance.

“All the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls.” Seventy souls went into Egypt, and this is Abraham's seed. Remember the Lord told Abraham that his seed would go into a strange land and be enslaved; here it begins.
“The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.” We became a nation within a nation.
“There arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph”, and he said unto his people, the Egyptians, “Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.”

“Come on, let us deal wisely with them.” So “they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens”: they set taskmasters over us and started afflicting us, and we built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

“But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew.” The more they afflict us, the more we multiply; we did not stop having children under affliction. “And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.” So we went into Egypt and started being afflicted there: we were enslaved in Egypt.
“I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” He lets Moses know: I am the God of your father Abraham, of Isaac and of Jacob.

“I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows.” The Lord tells Moses, I see the affliction of my people in Egypt, I hear them crying, I know their sorrows. So God rose up a prophet: he rose Moses up.

“I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians.” We went into Egypt as seventy souls, multiplied, became abundant and became a nation there. The Egyptians said, we have to deal wisely with these people, and made us their slaves and started oppressing us. Now God sends Moses to deliver us from ancient Egypt, “to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.”

“I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.” God saw the oppression and heard the cries. So don't think the Lord doesn't see when our people are being oppressed, and don't think God doesn't hear the cries.

“Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.” Moses is the prophet God rose up to deliver us out of the land of ancient Egypt.
“Israel is my son, even my firstborn.” God says Israel is his son, and his firstborn, because the firstborn gets the inheritance.

“Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.” And that is what ended up happening: the Lord killed every firstborn in Egypt, including Pharaoh's firstborn.
“Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year.” The lamb is to be without blemish, and a male lamb.

“Ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening.” The evening of the fourteenth day is the fifteenth day: that is the Passover, and that is what we celebrate this day.

“They shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses.” When you killed the lamb, you put the blood on your doorpost. But we do not do that today. There are brothers on YouTube killing a lamb and putting the blood on their doorposts; the scriptures show why we don't.

“They shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; and with bitter herbs they shall eat it.” Tonight we are to eat the lamb, with unleavened bread and with bitter herbs.

The bitter herbs represent the captivity, the bitter bondage we were in in Egypt: the bitter slavery, all the evil and bitterness we went through in ancient Egypt. The unleavened bread represents us without sin, or Christ without sin.

“Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast with fire; his head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof.” Don't eat it raw and don't boil it; roast it with fire, with everything in it. Even the roasting with fire is symbolic.

“With your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the Lord’s passover.” You are getting ready to make moves, ready to leave, with your staff in your hand, because the Lord is about to smite the Egyptians.

That is the Passover dinner: the night the Lord is about to pass over Egypt, smite and destroy the Egyptians, and deliver you out of captivity. That is why you eat it standing, staff in hand: the Lord is about to pass over.

“For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast.” Passover represents the Lord passing over the land of Egypt and killing all the firstborn. The Lord himself came down and did it.

Picture it: you wake up and every firstborn in America drops dead. Nobody knows what happened; hundreds of millions of people drop dead. That is the death and screaming of that night. “Against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the Lord.”

“The blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you.” The blood was a token. Even this is symbolic; that blood is pointing to something much heavier.

If you put the blood over your doorpost back then, it showed you believed the Lord. A Hebrew who said, I'm not putting any blood over my door, did not believe, and would have been killed along with the Egyptians.

“This day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the Lord throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.” It is something we must always remember, when God smote the ancient Egyptians and delivered us out of the land of ancient Egypt. That is why we are here.

Some think we are not supposed to keep the Passover or the holy days any more. No: we keep it as a feast throughout all our generations, for ever.

“Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread.” For seven days we eat no bread with leaven in it. “Whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” There is a lot to that: that soul will be cut off.

“No manner of work shall be done in them, save that which every man must eat.” This day is a day off. Some in captivity just got off work and have to go back tomorrow or lose the job; but those who have it in their power should take the day off, put it on the calendar and tell the boss. If he asks what you are talking about, take one of your sick days.
“For in this selfsame day have I brought your armies out of the land of Egypt.” In this same day God brought our armies out of the land of Egypt.

precepts.why:
“The Lord brought us forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with great terribleness, and with signs, and with wonders.” This is ancient Egypt: God brought us out of ancient Egypt with a mighty hand.

That great terribleness is the killing he did when he brought us out. He destroyed the Egyptians: he drowned them in the sea, killed all the firstborn, brought darkness on the land and a host of plagues on them to make them let us go out of slavery.

So with great terribleness and with signs the Lord brought us out of captivity, and “hath brought us into this place, and hath given us this land, even a land that floweth with milk and honey.”

sense.text: Some will ask why we eat lamb and keep the Passover today. “The first day of the feast of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?” The disciples came to Christ to prepare the Passover, meaning they ate lamb.
“I will keep the passover at thy house with my disciples.” Christ kept the Passover. “And they made ready the passover”: the lamb and the unleavened bread.
“Now when the even was come, he sat down with the twelve.” They made ready on the fourteenth; when the evening came, that is the fifteenth. “And as they did eat”, they ate the Passover dinner.
“Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.” The bread represents Christ's body.

“For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” The blood that we took and put on top of the doorpost in ancient Egypt represents Christ's blood: Christ coming and dying for our sins, and the new covenant.

So don't take blood and put it on the doorpost. Christ dying and shedding his blood for us is what that blood represented.

precepts.why:
John sees Jesus coming and says, “Behold the Lamb of God.” Christ is called the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year points to him: he is that sacrifice.

So we don't sacrifice any more, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God. Believing in Christ and doing what's right is what keeps you from the wrath of God.

“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.” The lamb that was killed represents Christ: he is our Passover, and that is saying a lot.

He was sacrificed for us; he came and died for our sins. So you don't have to go kill a lamb and put the blood over the doorpost so you don't die. You believe in Christ and keep the commandments, and we come together, break bread and drink wine. That is the new covenant.

sense.text: “If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.” When we came out of ancient Egypt we went into a covenant with the Lord, and he gave us commandments to keep. He said, if you do not keep my commandments, curses will come upon you, and those curses will destroy you.

precepts.why:
“Take this book of the law, and put it in the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there for a witness against thee. For I know thy rebellion, and thy stiff neck.” Moses says, I know you Israelites are rebellious, and you don't like listening. “While I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?”

“For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will befall you in the latter days.” The Lord used Moses to deliver us out of Egypt and to give us the laws, statutes and commandments: keep these things and everything goes well with you; don't, and bad things will happen to you.

Why could Moses say “I know”? Because God showed Moses what would happen to us in the last days. He showed him what happened to us in the time of the ancient Babylonians, the Greeks and the Romans, and Moses also saw us here in America.

“Ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.” When we went into the land of Israel our days would not be prolonged there; we would be destroyed off of that land.

“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” Moses saw the Israelites scattered to the four corners of the earth. He could tell us, I know that when you go into the land you will do evil and the Lord will put you out of it, because he saw it.

This is how Moses saw it. “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt”, when we were slaves in ancient Egypt. “And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt”: God sent Moses, and Moses led us out of ancient Egypt.

God brought him up to the mount, “where I held him by me a long season”, and that long season was forty days and forty nights. There he “told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end.”

Moses understood the secrets of the times, such as the beginning; that is how Moses could write Genesis, the beginning. And he saw the end. Moses saw the Romans, and he saw America: he saw America being destroyed and wrote about it in the law. He saw his people as slaves here in America. Moses saw the transatlantic slave trade.

sense.text:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships.” Moses prophesied that we would go into Egypt again, but this time with ships. What Moses is seeing is the transatlantic slave trade. Some say everybody went into slavery on ships at one time or another; no, this is the transatlantic slave trade, and this Egypt is not ancient Egypt.

“By the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again.” Moses is being very specific. He is saying, the Egypt I am naming is not that Egypt. The people would have said, Egypt again? Back into Egypt a second time? And he explains it: not the Egypt you just came out of, a different Egypt. Moses saw the end, and saw the Israelites brought here to America, thrown in cargo slave ships; the Lord showed it to him thousands of years ago.

Egypt comes from the Hebrew name Mizraim, which means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation and distress. So going into Egypt again with ships means going into a place of tribulation and misery, restrained, meaning captives, in distress. Egypt basically means oppression, misery and tribulation, and this time we would go into it with ships.

“And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” In this new Egypt we would be sold to our enemies, as slave men and slave women. This is the transatlantic slave trade.

precepts.why:
“Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.” The Bible says we would not see those Egyptians again, for ever.

So when the scripture says the Lord will bring us into Egypt again with ships, “by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”, it is not speaking of ancient Egypt. We were never going into ancient Egypt a second time. This is a new Egypt.

sense.text:
When Moses says we will go into slavery again with ships and be sold to our enemies, what is he talking about? “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” The their is the Israelites. Why dead bodies? Because we are spiritually dead, disconnected from our God: the twelve tribes of Israel.

That great city is Mystery Babylon the Great, and Mystery Babylon is America, the greatest country on this earth.

“Which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.” This place is spiritually Sodom and spiritually Egypt. The same spirit that was in Sodom and Gomorrah, the homosexuality and the lesbianism and all that filth, is the same spirit here in America. And the same spirit that was in ancient Egypt is the same spirit here in America.

Egypt means bondage, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. This place is called spiritual Egypt because the Israelites are here in America being oppressed: the same thing that happened to the Israelites in ancient Egypt happened to them here in America.

precepts.why:
“O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee.” When we sin against God, God refers to us as dead. Remember the scripture says, keep my commandments and live.

“And not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us.” That is why these plagues cleave unto us, and one of those plagues is us going into slavery on ships. The transatlantic slave trade was a plague, one of the curses of Deuteronomy 28.

“How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land”: now we are in our enemies' land. America is your enemies' land; they are the ones ruling this place. “That thou art waxen old in a strange country”, because our land is the land of Israel.

“That thou art defiled with the dead.” We walk around like zombies. We have broken God's laws and live in these lands not knowing who we are, confused, calling ourselves all kinds of names and titles. We are the congregation of the dead, the valley of dry bones: that is us today. That is why Revelation calls us dead bodies.

Where is that great city? “And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” That great city is Mystery Babylon, and Mystery Babylon is America, the greatest country on this earth. So the great city where the dead bodies of the Israelites lie, spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, is America.

sense.text:
Now to show that spiritual Egypt is America: the same thing that happened back then in ancient Egypt is the same thing that happened here in America. “All these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”, if we do not observe to keep all the commandments God gave us.

The curses of Deuteronomy 28 did not come out of nowhere. A lot of them were the same curses that were on us in ancient Egypt. So when the scripture says America is spiritually called Egypt, it is because the same things that happened to us in ancient Egypt happened to us here. Read the curses of Deuteronomy 28, then read what happened to us in ancient Egypt, and you will see it is the same thing.

precepts.why: “The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, and with the emerods, and with the scab, and with the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed.” The curses are named after Egypt: the botch of Egypt.

“Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee.” All the diseases of Egypt, the very things we were afraid of, would cleave unto us. Those curses were some of the same curses that were on us in ancient Egypt.

sense.text: “Now therefore, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: and I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.” The Lord says, I see the oppression. Our forefathers were oppressed in ancient Egypt, our forefathers were oppressed here in America, and we are still being oppressed here in America. The oppression is real.

precepts.why:
This is one of the curses that fell upon us. “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”: we as a nation of people would not prosper in our ways.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore.” We would always be oppressed and spoiled. That is the oppression God saw in Egypt, and the same oppression is upon us here.

sense.text: “Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.” This is what Pharaoh said: the children of Israel are more and mightier than us.

“Come on, let us deal wisely with them.” That dealing wisely is institutional slavery being set up: setting up slavery and institutionalizing it to oppress us, keep our people destroyed and bring affliction on our people. Let us enslave them, make them servants, keep them down in society, set up institutions where they can't own this and can't do that.

The same thing that happened to us in ancient Egypt happened to us in America. That is why this place is spiritually called Egypt.

“Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” The taskmasters today are the governors, politicians, police officers and FBI agents, the people set to keep us in check and keep us in order. They set up laws to keep us low, institutional laws like Jim Crow and the black codes, back then and also today in America.

Back then there were Egyptian taskmasters; on the cotton field there was always a white overseer the slave master put over us to make sure we did the work, and if you didn't you got your ass whooped. Today your taskmaster is your boss, making sure you do what you are supposed to do.

“And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.” We built cities in ancient Egypt, and it is the same thing here in America.

“But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew.” We keep multiplying and growing no matter how much they afflict us. “And they were grieved because of the children of Israel”: they were mad, they were angry; they hated us.

“And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour”: hard bondage. “And they made their lives bitter”, and the bitter herbs we eat tonight represent our lives made bitter in Egypt.

“In morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field.” We were doing brickwork, and we were in the fields in ancient Egypt; we were not just building pyramids. They had us doing plantation work and cropping there; it was not bricklaying and building cities alone. You had five-year-olds and two-year-olds picking cotton here.

All manner of service: we were their servants, cooking their food and watching their kids, in Egypt and in America. It goes into music too: we entertain them, and perform for them. Sing me one of the songs of Zion: that is what we do here in Babylon.

We have been slaves so long that we got comfortable with the jobs they give us: driving a bus, fixing the road for the DOT, driving taxi cabs, the civil servant job with twenty days off a year, and calling ourselves free. That is all manner of service. We are kings and priests; we are not supposed to serve any nation. Our job is to serve God, nobody else.

“All their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.” Whatever the Egyptians needed, we provided, because we were their slaves, and they ruled over us with rigour. The same way the white man ruled over us with rigour: he lynched us and still lynches us, and when the slaves ran away he caught them and whipped them. In ancient Egypt they beat the hell out of us with whips, and then we came to America and they did the same thing to us. Not only America: all these lands we were scattered into are Egypt, but this is the main one, Mystery Babylon. We toted water for them and planted crops for them. Everything we did back then in ancient Egypt we are doing today.

“When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him.” Once it was a male, Pharaoh said kill that baby. That is oppression, and America is doing the same thing.

precepts.why:
“The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low.” The strangers are the people who were among us. To be above us means they rule and tell us what to do, and that is also called a taskmaster.

“He shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.” That curse was on us in ancient Egypt: the Egyptians were over us and we were at the bottom of society. It is the same way the so-called white man and the nations are above us today, and we are at the bottom of society.

“Thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein.” One of the curses in ancient Egypt is that we built cities and houses, and not for ourselves: we built them for the Egyptians. It is the same thing in modern-day Egypt, spiritual Egypt.

The White House was built by enslaved people, hundreds of them rented from plantation owners: they quarried the stone, cut the timber, laid the bricks and carved the columns, dawn to dusk, no wages, and when it was finished they were sent back to the plantations. Some thought the white man built that. What house did we build here in America and were not able to dwell in? The White House.

“Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her”: that was the same in ancient Egypt too. In ancient Egypt we were slaves, a commodity; they did not look at us as human, and America did the same thing. We built cities in Egypt and did not dwell in them either.

This explains “they were grieved because of the children of Israel”. “I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you.” To be grieved because of us means they hated us.

The same way the ancient Egyptians hated us, the so-called white man hates us since we were brought here as slaves. America is spiritually called Egypt: the same thing ancient Egypt did to us is what America did and is doing to us.

“Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.” The same way they made us slaves in ancient Egypt and made us work in the fields and in all manner of service, that curse fell upon us in America. We were cursed in the cotton field, the sugar cane field and the tobacco field.

How were we cursed in the field? Exodus 1:14: they made our lives bitter with hard bondage, in all manner of service in the field. We were cursed in the field because we were slaves. America is spiritual Egypt: the same things the Egyptians did to us are the same things the white man did to us.

“Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body.” The fruit of our body is our children. In ancient Egypt the midwives were commanded to kill the male child as it was born; today they do the same thing, and it is called abortion.

How do they get rid of the male today? The school-to-prison pipeline. They create a condition of poverty for our people, bring drugs into the community, and put the brothers who sell them away for the rest of their lives. That whole system was set up by Esau. That is them dealing wisely with us.

Also through the vaccines, which target the boys: look at how high the rate of autism is among young black and Hispanic men. They put things in the vaccines to mess with the babies' minds. They have things that can attack a certain type of DNA, but Esau has been mixing with us, so some of our DNA is in theirs, and now white people complain their kids are coming out with autism too. It is too late.

That goes back to the scripture that says they try to destroy the poor secretly. Secretly they try to kill every male child among us, because they are trying to stop the prophets from coming on the earth.

sense.text: “He spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.” Moses saw one of his brethren being smitten by an Egyptian.

“When he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.” Some might say Moses was a murderer. He didn't kill out of hatred. Moses did what brothers did in the time of the Black Panthers. In the '60s and '70s racist cops were killing our people and we were being oppressed, the same thing that went on in ancient Egypt, and brothers rose up: you kill one of us, we kill one of yours. There are men locked up in prison right now who are prisoners of war for rising up. That is the spirit Moses was rolling in.

“Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian?” They knew. So Moses was out; he fled. You try to help them and they will turn on you just like that.

This is the curse our people are under today, and this is what Moses saw. “Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart.” We have a trembling heart because we are scared for our lives, in ancient Egypt and in this Egypt.

“Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life.” You don't know if you are going to live today or die tomorrow. That is the power the white man had over our lives, and the power the ancient Egyptians had over our lives. That is how bad the oppression was.

“And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves.” This shows there was segregation in ancient Egypt: No Hebrews allowed. The same way there is segregation here in spiritual Egypt, America.

“Because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” The Egyptians ate by themselves. The same way in America the white man didn't want you eating in his restaurants; you came to the back to order your food. They hated us so much they said, we don't want to eat with you niggers. White people will literally say they hate us and don't want to sit and eat with us. It is the same spirit that was in ancient Egypt.

We lived in Goshen; we did not live among the Egyptians. We went there to work and serve them. They dealt wisely with us and set up institutional slavery for us, and we cried out to the Lord, and he sent Moses and delivered us out of ancient Egypt.

“And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again.” “We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick.” The Nile was abundant in fish and we had melons; brothers were delivered from oppression and were talking about going back to Egypt, saying at least there we got some good food.

It is the same with us here in America: a lot of us have food and are full. For now.

precepts.why:
“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” That is one of the curses upon us, and it was also on us in ancient Egypt: we had to serve the Egyptians for the want of all things.

The Egyptians fed us, and the same is true today: you need money to buy food, so you have to serve for it.

Not only did the Egyptians feed us; everything we learned, we learned from the Egyptians. “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.” When we came out, God said don't do after the doings of Egypt, because we had learned the Egyptian customs, the Egyptian names of the days of the week.

It is the same here in America with Monday and Tuesday and all of that: it is all idolatry. God says, everything you learned in Egypt, forget it, and it will be the same when he delivers us from here.

sense.text:
“By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God.” Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter, and chose rather to suffer affliction with the people of God.

In ancient Egypt everybody wasn't bad off. Things weren't bad for Moses; Moses made things bad for himself by killing the Egyptian. There were laws, and a consequence or death penalty for killing an Egyptian, so Moses was on the run.

precepts.why:
“And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten.” There were officers of the children of Israel set over us by the taskmasters. In America they are called Uncle Tom Negroes, house Negroes; in ancient Egypt they were the officers the taskmasters set up over us. And they started getting beaten too.

So some of our people in ancient Egypt had money and high standing, a form of good living, and were okay with the oppression. It is the same today: Beyoncé, Usher, the pastor praying for Trump, people with money who are comfortable in modern-day Egypt, spiritual Egypt. Moses refused all that and chose to suffer with his people.

When you live under oppression for a while, it becomes the norm. When our people live in oppression for centuries, it becomes a way of life. That is why the scripture speaks of us trusting in the shadow of Egypt, trusting in oppression.

sense.text: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that they shall no more say, The Lord liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.” A day is coming when it will no longer be said that the Lord delivered us out of the land of Egypt, which is what we celebrate today.

“But, The Lord liveth, which brought up and which led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country, and from all countries whither I had driven them; and they shall dwell in their own land.” The Lord will deliver us out of the north country and from all the countries he drove us into as slaves, and put us back in our own land.

The land of the north is spiritual Egypt. North of Jerusalem was Babylon, but it is worded that way for a reason: he is speaking of Mystery Babylon the Great. God is going to deliver us from here.

precepts.why: “The great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.” Why is that great city spiritually called Egypt? Because the same things that happened in ancient Egypt happened here, and the same things that happened in Sodom and Gomorrah are happening here. That is the Egypt the new deliverance comes out of: the north country, Mystery Babylon the Great.

sense.text:
Now Moses speaks of us being here in America, and of America being destroyed. “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”: we go into Egypt a second time, with ships, and Moses is letting us know he is not talking about ancient Egypt.

“And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”: sold unto our enemies, the so-called white man, as slave men and slave women.

“And no man shall buy you”: nobody would be able to save us. The word buy there means redeem. In slavery back then someone could have come and paid a price to redeem you; that is why Christ is called our redeemer, and we are purchased with his blood.

That is the last curse that was to come upon us. And did Moses speak of us being in this Egypt? The next chapter shows it.

Did Moses speak of us being in this Egypt? Go to the next chapter. “Ye have seen all that the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt unto Pharaoh, and unto all his servants, and unto all his land; The great temptations which thine eyes have seen, the signs, and those great miracles.” They saw the destruction of Egypt; they saw the sea open up and kill everybody.
“Yet the Lord hath not given you an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.” And still they did not want to repent.

“I have led you forty years in the wilderness: your clothes are not waxen old upon you, and thy shoe is not waxen old upon thy foot.” Wearing the same clothes for forty years and they never got old: that is something spiritual, and heavy.

“Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath; But with him that standeth here with us this day before the Lord our God, and also with him that is not here with us this day.” The covenant is also with those not there that day: us in the future. You can't say, I wasn't there when you made the covenant with God. Moses says the covenant is not only for those standing before him but for their descendants.
“For ye know how we have dwelt in the land of Egypt”: we dwelt in ancient Egypt, and came through the nations and saw “their abominations, and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold.”
“Whose heart turneth away this day from the Lord our God, to go and serve the gods of these nations”: you go and serve Christianity, or call yourself a Muslim.

“When he heareth the words of this curse.” If the curse was being taught to them back then, why say when he hears it? It is prophetic. Moses is saying, what I am telling you is not only for you in front of me but for those who come in the future. When you hear the words of this curse is us teaching on the street; at one point all of us heard this truth.

“That he bless himself in his heart, saying, I shall have peace, though I walk in the imagination of mine heart.” I am at peace; I'm good being a Muslim, I'm good being a Christian; what are these Israelites talking about? That is what a lot of our people say here in spiritual Egypt. Walking in the imagination of your heart is imagining Jesus Christ is a white man and following that, or imagining the Lord is dealing with Ishmael and being a Muslim, while hearing the teaching that you are the Israelites and the curses of God came upon you.

“The Lord will not spare him.” This is speaking of now, the future; Moses saw the future. “All the curses that are written in this book shall lie upon him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven.” Any of our people who hear the words of this covenant and the curses and reject it, the Lord says, I will blot their name out of the book: every Israelite here in Egypt who rejects this truth.
“And the Lord shall separate him unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel.” This is something heavy: judgment in the future.

“So that the generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you” is speaking of those of us who make it to the kingdom.

“When they see the plagues of that land.” Some think Moses is speaking of Israel; no, he is speaking of Egypt, spiritual Egypt, America. Moses saw America destroyed with thermonuclear destruction and recorded it here. “And the sicknesses which the Lord hath laid upon it”: the sickness the Lord laid upon America.

And not only destroyed: America will be the place where all the evil, wicked demons are kept. Remember the demons said, art thou come to torment us before our time? That place of torment will be set up here. After this place is destroyed physically, a spiritual prison and damnation will be set up here.

“The whole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, and burning, that it is not sown, nor beareth, nor any grass groweth therein.” This is that land of Deuteronomy 28:68, the land we were slaves in, being destroyed.

“Like the overthrow of Sodom, and Gomorrah.” Remember this place is called Sodom. The same way Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed with fire, spiritually this place will be destroyed with fire, when Christ returns in the new Passover.

“Even all nations shall say, Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land?” The nations that are left in the future will look upon America and say it. “Because they have forsaken the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers, which he made with them when he brought them forth out of the land of Egypt.” We came out of Egypt, the Lord made a covenant with us, and we broke it. Moses is going over the judgment for our people who don't repent in America, and not only America being destroyed but torment.

“For they went and served other gods, and worshipped them, gods whom they knew not.” “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against this land, to bring upon it all the curses that are written in this book.” Remember Revelation 11:8 calls this place spiritually Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified: all that judgment is coming down on America.

“And the Lord rooted them out of their land in anger, and in wrath, and in great indignation”: now it is speaking of the land of Israel, and the great indignation is 70 AD. “And cast them into another land, as it is this day.” That other land is the land of Deuteronomy 28:68, the land that was burning in the verses above.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us.” This is the secret thing Moses understood: that we would be brought into spiritual Egypt, into America, and he saw America being destroyed.

precepts.why:
Who is the generation to come of thy children that shall rise up after thee? “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” The seed and name that remain in that new heaven and new earth are the righteous of our people who make it.

“Shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord. And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me.” After they come up to worship, they go forth and look on this place, America. If a carcass is supposed to just disappear after death, this lets you know it is something spiritual; that is why it says the Lord will separate the man who did not repent unto evil.

“For their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched.” They are in damnation, cast into hell, being tormented. There is a place of torment, and it will be set up when Christ returns. Christ has the power over hell and death: he can wake you up and torment you, or give you life, immortality.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.” Many are going to awake: some to everlasting life, some to shame and everlasting contempt.

When you die you go to sleep, yes, but Christ has the power to wake your behind up and torment you. That is the man the Lord separates unto evil.

“Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils.” This is what Moses spoke of: America is fallen and has become the habitation of devils.

“And the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.” A hold is like a prison. After America is destroyed, America will become a prison, a cage, a hold.

“For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.” The she inhabited by devils is America. This place will be the place of torment, the prison of the same devils who said, art thou come to torment us before our time.

When America is destroyed and Christ returns, he is going to set up a lake of fire here, spiritual damnation in America for all the wicked. That great time is a thousand years.

“And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it.” You hated God's laws while you had liberty, while the place of repentance was open to you, and that is today.

“The same must know it after death by pain.” You are going to understand God's laws after death, by pain. That shows Christ has power over your spirit when you die; that is why Christ said not to fear him who can destroy the flesh, but to fear him who has power over your soul. Christ has the power over hell and death, to torment your spirit and destroy it.

If our people do not repent and still worship the beast and his image, they will feel pain after death, and that pain is burning, fire.

sense.text:
Deuteronomy 28 goes into the curses that fell on us in ancient Egypt, and 28:68 is the last curse: us coming into spiritual Egypt, America. Deuteronomy 29 goes into America being destroyed and hell being set up here, with the wicked Israelites who don't repent. Deuteronomy 30 goes into us getting back the kingdom of heaven, after the destruction.

“When all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before thee, and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee.” Calling them to mind among all the nations is what we are doing right now.

“And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul.” That is what we are doing right now: returning unto the Lord and obeying his voice.

“That then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath scattered thee.” We are still this day in the land of our captivity. When we turn to God with all our heart, soul and mind, he will turn our captivity.

That is the new Passover: the Lord coming, destroying our enemies and delivering us out of here, gathering us from wherever we were scattered.
“From thence will the Lord thy God gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee”: bring my sons from far.

“And the Lord thy God will bring thee into the land which thy fathers possessed, and thou shalt possess it.” Moses saw America destroyed, and he saw us back in the land. He saw it all, and he is letting us know.

“And the Lord thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love the Lord thy God with all thine heart.” He will take away that stony heart, that wicked, evil mind, and we will truly love the Lord and never go against him or rebel against him again. This is us back in the land, the kingdom of heaven.

“And the Lord thy God will put all these curses upon thine enemies, and on them that hate thee.” Moses saw the curses upon our enemies: they will have the yokes of iron upon their necks; they will be at the bottom and we at the top. All the curses that were upon us go upon them, upon all the nations that hate us. The white man who hates us, the curse is going to be on him.

precepts.why:
What has to happen for God to gather us? We have to turn to him with all our heart, soul and mind, and right now a lot of us are comfortable. “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face.” The Lord went back to the heavens until we acknowledge what we did wrong to end up where we are, enslaved and destroyed as a people.

“In their affliction they will seek me early.” We will seek God with all our heart, soul and mind in affliction. A lot of us are comfortable in America, but affliction is about to be turned up on all of us. After the '60s we got civil rights and the liberal things in America, and they are taking it away, taking it back.

“The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt.” He comes riding as on a chariot. Why is the Lord coming into Egypt? The new Passover: the same way he went into Egypt the first time to get us, to deliver us.

This is not ancient Egypt; the Lord never went back a second time into ancient Egypt. It is spiritual Egypt, the Egypt we are in right now, Mystery Babylon the Great. “And the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence”: Christ is going to destroy all the idols they have here.

“In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan.” Speaking the language of Canaan is us prophesying and teaching the word of God: five cities with brothers going in hard teaching the word. “One shall be called, The city of destruction”: much destruction will take place.

“In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt.” That altar is affliction: brothers dying for this truth. In your affliction you will seek me. We have to cry out the same way we cried out in Exodus, when the Lord heard us as the Egyptians afflicted us, and the same thing is about to take place here in Babylon.

“For they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.” So much will happen to our people, affliction and tribulation, which is what Egypt means, that we will cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors: the white man, the ADL, the US government.

“And he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.” He will send Christ, who is coming back on this earth to deliver us from spiritual Egypt. That is why it will no more be said that the Lord liveth who delivered the children of Israel from the land of Egypt: they will be delivered from spiritual Egypt, Mystery Babylon the Great, America.

“And the Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day”: the Egyptians there are you brothers and sisters living in the land of Egypt, the land of America. “And the Lord shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal it.” That goes into the affliction we are going through, and healing us, because we will change. As God brings plagues on Babylon, on America, many of our people will change.

“Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” “And their hurtful works are fulfilled”: all the hurtful things the white man has done on this earth are fulfilled.

“I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickedness, which they profanely commit, neither will I suffer them in those things, in which they wickedly exercise themselves.” The things Esau exercises himself in, the Lord says, I won't allow any more, and some of those things are the killing and afflicting of the children of Israel. The same way they afflicted and killed us in ancient Egypt is going to take place here in the future.

“Behold, the innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me, and the souls of the just complain continually.” A lot of blood is going to be shed here in Babylon, and it will cry out to the Lord the same way we cried out in ancient Egypt. When we die, we are with the Lord saying, Lord, when are you going to bring vengeance on these white people for what they did to us? “I will surely avenge them.” “My people is led as a flock to the slaughter”, which is what they are going to be doing to us here in Babylon.

“I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt.” Which Egypt? America. “But I will bring them with a mighty hand and a stretched out arm”: this is the new Exodus. “And smite Egypt with plagues, as before.” As before lets you know this is not ancient Egypt: the same way he smote ancient Egypt with plagues, he will do the same to this spiritual Egypt, America, where his people were slaves.

“And will destroy all the land thereof.” The land of ancient Egypt was not destroyed; this is Mystery Babylon, spiritual Egypt, America. “Egypt shall mourn, and the foundation of it shall be smitten with the plague and punishment that God shall bring upon it.” God is bringing punishment and plague upon this land.

“My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God.” The wrath that came upon us from God is slavery, the curses of Deuteronomy 28. “For thine enemy hath persecuted thee”: our enemies enslaved us and persecute us. “But shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.” We are going to see our enemies destroyed. There is no salvation unless your enemies are destroyed; some want to take their enemies into the kingdom of heaven with them. No.

When they afflict you, put you in prison for things you didn't do, lie on you and bring charges against you for the word of God's sake, remember that shortly you will see his destruction. Even if you die today or tomorrow you will see it, because the Lord is going to bring you back. The new Passover is a resurrection too: not only the Lord coming and destroying, but bringing souls back with him.

“Be of good comfort, O my children, and cry unto God”: Jerusalem is speaking, and this is what God wants us to do, cry unto him. We haven't started crying yet because we are not being afflicted. In the 1800s, during Jim Crow, when we were being lynched, we were crying; but the white man gave us sixty years of civil rights and a false sense of comfort. The Lord has sent Trump, and other presidents will rise after him who will turn up affliction on our people, and we will cry.

“So, being returned, seek him ten times more.” We have to seek God ten times more. “For he that hath brought these plagues upon you shall bring you everlasting joy with your salvation.” The plagues are the curses of Deuteronomy 28, and with that salvation we will have everlasting joy.

“Miserable are they that afflicted thee, and rejoiced at thy fall.” Everyone who afflicted us and took us as slaves, and rejoiced when we fell as a nation. “Miserable are the cities which thy children served”: every city where we were slaves and served in hard bondage will be in misery, every last one of them, including the United States of America. “Miserable is she that received thy sons”: she is Egypt, America, and thy sons are the Israelites who came here as slaves and served hard bondage here in Egypt.

“So shall she be grieved for her own desolation. For I will take away the rejoicing of her great multitude, and her pride shall be turned into mourning.” This is spiritual Egypt, America: there will be no more rejoicing here, and everybody here will be mourning. That is future prophecy. “For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.”

“Lo, thy sons come, whom thou sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.”

sense.text:
What is taking place with the brothers out on the missions is prophecy. “How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?” All the people around the world do not believe in the Christ of the Bible. “And how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” They never heard the true gospel that is being taught right now: that they are the Israelites, that Christ is a black man, and that he came to deliver them out of the land of their captivity.

“And how shall they hear without a preacher?” All the brothers all over the world, the soldiers, officers and captains, are the teachers, and the only way people will hear is for the teachers to go and teach. We will not cover all the earth, but we will wake up who the Lord wants us to wake up, those that are left.

“And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” To preach you have to be taught and you have to be sent. “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” That is what the brothers are doing right now.
